title: I’ve been building a turn-based tactics game in a world where you can send your mind back in time. Looking for feedback.
author: schiehll
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’ve started learning how to code 15+ years ago to build games. I went to game dev school back then, built my own engine, built some games for fun here and there, and even made some money with it.  
  
But I ended up spending my whole career as a software engineer building web apps, so building games became a hobby.  
  
Now, 15 years later, I’m finally releasing my first game on Steam!  
  
Here’s the Steam Page for it (I would really appreciate a wishlist there!): [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5587330/The\_Backwave/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5587330/The_Backwave/)  
  
I’m looking for feedback on the trailer, the game idea, the screenshots, or even the Steam Page itself. Good or bad!  
  
It’s the first time people are seeing it outside of me and my wife (she says she likes it, but I know she loves me so that doesn’t count), so anything helps.  
  
It’s built on a custom engine written in Rust on top of Bevy ECS.  
The cars and guns are paid assets.  
The people are MetaHumans.  
Music created on Suno.  
SFX created with a local model.  
Some VFX are paid assets as well.  
Everything else was built assisted by Claude (Opus 5.5 for the majority of it) using code and Blender.

replies.author: schiehll
replies.body:
You mean if there are different classes you can choose?

Not really. The idea of the game is that you can send your mind back in time, and for every mission you go you need to pick a host for you mind (you can pick host for your companions as well - companions can be synthetic minds that you train on your rig with the skills you like).   
  
Every host has 2 good traits and 1 bad one, and their age and build also influence on how good or bad they are (HP, movement, aim). The host options are random every mission, so no mission plays exactly the same twice.

comments.author: drahgon
comments.body:
Looks great, but the music made this trailer good. The concept sounds cool, but I just don’t feel like I understand the game enough from the trailer or what’s going on. I’ll still probably wishlist it because it looks pretty cool. Maybe some kind of cinematics-type trailer with words on screen or something explaining the mind transfer mechanic. This is a movie-quality storyline like I want to watch the movie of this concept as a sci-fi fan. I think that would really bring across the concept better. Then you could have this be your second gameplay trailer.

For example, there’s towards the end of your trailer you have a part where there’s a girl dancing and that looks cinematic level. That’s the kind of graphics I think you should shoot for but for the whole trailer.

Also, really don’t like the Steam page cover graphic. Don’t think it does the game justice just looks a bit generic.

replies.author: schiehll
replies.body:
Thank you so much for taking the time to give feedback!

I’m honestly not 100% happy with the capsule on the steam page neither! I will look into making it better.

I was also not sure if the trailer would make the game clear. I left a lot of things out as i didn’t think people would watch more than a minute and a half, but in the end i think i still ended up putting too much there and made it confusing.

I’m not a big fan of cinematic trailers as i want to see gameplay myself when i look into other games, but maybe you are right, maybe it’s what i need to explain the concept a bit better.

Thank you again!

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body:
No problem. I just wouldn’t ignore how much this game is laid out as an awesome time based movie, like tenant or inception. It’s got a lot of movie quality to it already. And if you don’t have a lot of in game cinematics I feel like it would also benefit from them. And you could maybe then reuse it in your trailer.

Good luck. Excited to see where it goes.

replies.author: schiehll
replies.body:
i currently have one cinematic at the start of each mission, even the non main story ones. But they are mostly for a cool effect, I will think more about using them to tell the story!

Thank you!

replies.author: pixelvspixel
replies.body:
I agree with you. It looks great, I can tell lots of love and work went into it. Made me think of the old game Syndicate from 1996. It did have that feeling of AI/Claude over complicating things in some places, but I get the theme is meant to be a bit technical. 

I actually went back and watched the trailer again from my PC after reading your comment. 

I think it's a nice concept for a trailer, but something is off about it. I'm guessing you worked with Claude to cut it. Some of the edits don't really make sense and the end just feels like it fades out. I really loved the scene of the Ferris wheel falling after the van back into it. If I had been cutting, I would have pulled the camera in close on a few of those shots and cut to the beat a bit more.  I'd also consider cutting a shorter, tighter version that sells the gameplay loop in an explicit package.

Good luck op!

replies.author: Redditry199
replies.body: I am working on a similar-ish game, I'd recommend oval opacity(like in the original fallouts) for units so theyre not always obscured, lighting the units so they pop more and tricks like that because they just blend way too well in with the background. You really should go for a readability pass, what your eyes can see on a screen within a second, because right now its just too much noise and little clarity, that's what I think your biggest issue is.
